synopsis: Liz Twist is the Labour MP for Blaydon and Consett, and has been an MP continually since 8 June 2017.

history.heading: Special Educational Needs: Surveys
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Education, if she will make an assessment of the potential merits of including acquired brain injury as a specific category in the special educational needs survey.

history.heading: Poverty: Children
history.questionText: To ask the Minister for Women and Equalities, what steps she is taking with Cabinet colleagues to help reduce levels of inequality for children in poverty.

history.heading: Respiratory Diseases: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, what estimate his Department has made of the potential impact of increasing national pulmonary rehabilitation referral rates on (a) clinical outcomes for patients, (b) NHS emergency admission rates
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Respiratory Diseases: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, what steps he is taking to help improve the 37% referral rates of eligible patients for pulmonary rehabilitation.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Respiratory Diseases: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, whether he make an assessment of the potential merits of a Modern Service Framework for respiratory health to help improve referral and take up rates of pulmonary rehabilitation.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Health Services
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, what steps are being taken to improve access to pulmonary rehabilitation for adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease living in Blaydon and Consett constituency.
history.answeringBodyName: Department of Health and Social Care

history.heading: Living Wage and Minimum Wage
history.questionText: To ask the Secretary of State for Business and Trade, what progress he has made with Cabinet colleagues on helping reduce the number of employers underpaying the National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage.

To ask the Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, with reference to point 5 of HM Treasury's document entitled The Data Centre Covenant, published on 28 October 2026, how the compute for public services will be secured.
history.answeringBodyName: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
